Rotura marginal del cuerpo del menisco medial con mínima extrusión.

dentro de límites normales.

Rotura compleja del menisco lateral con extrusión asociada.
Rotura marginal del cuerpo del menisco medial con mínima extrusión.
Condropatía con lesiones grado 3 y 4 del compartimento femorotibial lateral. Condropatía con
lesiones grado 1 y 2 de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial.

MRI LEFT KNEE  (plain)

Clinical information:
Locked knee, history of ACL tear

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
Prior MRI dated [Date]

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: intact

Medial meniscus: Complex tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with extension to the inferior articular surface. Radial tear of the anterior horn is also seen. No para meniscal cyst.

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: Previous edema has resolved. At most low grade tear. Posterior cruciate ligament: intact 

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. No periligamentous edema.

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is normally positioned within the femoral groove. There is no retinacular disruption.

Fluid

No joint effusion or loose body. No Baker's cyst.

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Mild chondrosis.

Medial compartment: Minimal chondrosis

Lateral compartment: Minimal chondrosis

Others:

Hoffa's fat pad: clear

Muscles: No abnormal oedema. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT
Complex tear of the medial meniscus involving the body, anterior and posterior horns.
Low grade tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.

FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Minor joint effusion. Small popliteal cyst, leaking fluid, with sliver of fluid accumulating around the medial gastrocnemius and semimembranosus muscles.. The cyst measures 1.3 cm x 0.6 cm x 3.6 cm. There is also mild distention of the semimembranosus bursa.. 5 mm ganglion cyst anterior to the proximal tibiofibular joint.

There is edema adjacent to the posterior joint capsule and in the popliteal fossa.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
There is a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus, derived from the anterior horn, body and posterior horn, with the meniscal flap located in the intercondylar notch. There is tearing of the residual peripheral body and posterior horn, within main horizontal oblique component surfacing inferiorly.
There is a mild cartilage thinning and partial-thickness fissuring at the medial compartment. There are no reactive subchondral marrow changes.
Medial collateral ligament complex is intact. Ganglion cyst changes in the tibial attachment of the semimembranosus.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Lateral meniscus is normal. Lateral supporting structures are intact. Mild cartilage thinning at the weightbearing surface of the lateral femoral condyle. No full-thickness cartilage loss.


Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Normal.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Normal.

Bones:
Normal.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:

There is a extensive a bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus derived from the anterior horn, body and posterior horn, with a displaced meniscal flap in the intercondylar notch. The residual peripheral medial meniscus demonstrates horizontal oblique tearing in the body and posterior horn.

Small popliteal cyst, with leakage of fluid proximally and distally.

Mild distention of the semimembranosus bursa.

Mild chondropathy at the femoral condyles.

Posterior soft tissue edema, likely in part related to the fluid leakage from the popliteal cyst and joint, but also could be related to the injury..

Orthopedic consultation recommended.

Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: [REDACTED]. No known injury.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Normal background marrow signal. No focal osseous lesion.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: No tear.
Medial compartment cartilage: Intact.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: No tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Intact.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Diffuse articular cartilage irregularity. High-grade articular cartilage loss of the medial patellar facet. Areas of full-thickness chondral fissuring and delamination at the lateral facet with associated subchondral signal changes.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. Patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 9 mm, normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Features of lateral patellofemoral maltracking, including superolateral Hoffa's fat pad impingement and moderate patellofemoral chondrosis.
2.	Small knee joint effusion.

MRI of left Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS, Locator, AX T2W FS


> Obliteration of anterior horn of lateral meniscus, reflecting tear.
> Wearing of articular cartilage of left knee with spur formation, more severe at left compartement with subchondral bone marrow edema and tiny cyst over lateral femorotibial joint.
> Deep fissure in lateral facet of patella, reflecting grade 3 patellar chondromalacia.
> Mild interstitial increased signal intensit of ACL and PCL on F/S T2WI, in favor of grade 1 injury. 
> No evidence of tear in medial meniscus.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar, lateral and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
  Mild fat stranding over infrapatellar fat pad.
> A lobulated cystic lesion in medial popliteal fossa between the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius and the semimembranosus muscles, in favor of Baker's cyst.
> Abnormal signal intensity of disltal femoral shaft, most due to post-operative bone marrow change ( removal of internal fixation)

Impression: 
1. Tear of anterior horn of lateral meniscus.
2. Osteoarthritis of left knee, more severe at lateral compartment wtih grade 4 injury.
3. Grade 3 patellar chondromalcia.
4. Grade 1 injury of ACL and PCL.
5. Synovitis of left knee and mild suprapatellar bursitis and patellar plicae and small Baker's cyst.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Gonalgia y coxalgia en estudio.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
El menisco lateral es de morfología y señal conservada, sin signos de rotura.
Aumento de señal del cuerno posterior y cuerpo del menisco medial que contacta la superficie articular
inferior compatible una rotura, con pequeño componente desplazado hacia región intercondílea posterior de
manera, laminar. Podría existir compromiso parcial de la raíz meniscal posterior. Pequeña formación
quística de 5 x 6 mm adyacente al cuerno posterior del menisco medial, sugiriendo pequeño quiste
parameniscal.
Cartílagos de los compartimentos femorotibiales y de la tróclea femoral sin alteraciones. Úlceras condrales
de espesor parcial del vértice y faceta medial de la rótula, sin cambios óseos secundarios.
No hay derrame articular y quistes poplíteos patológicos.
Leve aumento de señal del tercio distal del tendón cuadricipital, sin signos de rotura. Discreto edema el
paquete adiposo retro cuadricipital suprarrotuliano, probablemente reactivo. Tendón rotuliano, tendones de
la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites normales.
Edema las partes blandas entre la banda iliotibial y el cóndilo femoral lateral que sugieran fenómenos de
fricción regional.
Impresión:
Signos sugerentes una rotura del menisco medial con laminar componente parcialmente desplazado hacia
la región intercondílea posterior y quiste parameniscal posterior.
Tendinosis cuadricipital distal con discreto edema el paquete adiposo retro cuadricipital suprarrotuliano de
manera reactiva.
Probables fenómenos de fricción de la banda iliotibial.
Condropatía lesiones grado dos y tres de la rótula
